# TDMM

TDMM fits Bayesian time-dynamic mixed-effects models for longitudinal
**Gaussian, Bernoulli, and Poisson** outcomes. It estimates time-varying
coefficient functions with subject-specific random intercepts. Data may
have irregular subject-specific observation times, unequal visit counts,
baseline covariates, and covariates that vary by visit.

The default spline uses **eight cubic B-spline basis functions**
(polynomial degree 3, spline order 4) with a second-order
coefficient-difference penalty. JAGS performs posterior sampling.

## Install

Install [JAGS](https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io/) first, then install
TDMM in R:

``` r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM")
library(TDMM)
```

## Fit a model

Supply one row per observed visit. Here `baseline` is constant within
subject and `changing` varies by visit:

``` r
fit <- tdmm(long_data, family = "gaussian",
            subject.var = "id", time.var = "time", y.var = "y",
            x.var = c("baseline", "changing"), n_basis = 8,
            control = tdmm_control(chains = 3, seed = 123))
summary(fit)
plot(fit)
plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "sigma2.e", "tau.alpha[1]"))
```

Use `family = "bernoulli"` for binary outcomes or `family = "poisson"`
for counts. See [Getting
Started](https://esrakurum.github.io/Bayesian-TDMM/articles/getting-started.html)
for data layout, interpretation, and diagnostics. The
[Gaussian](https://esrakurum.github.io/Bayesian-TDMM/articles/gaussian.html),
[Bernoulli](https://esrakurum.github.io/Bayesian-TDMM/articles/bernoulli.html),
[Poisson](https://esrakurum.github.io/Bayesian-TDMM/articles/poisson.html),
and [PBC2](https://esrakurum.github.io/Bayesian-TDMM/articles/pbc2.html)
examples give fuller workflows. The [vignette
source](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/blob/main/vignettes/getting-started.Rnw)
and [example
scripts](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/tree/main/examples)
are also available in the repository.

## Citation

For v0.2.0, use `citation("TDMM")` or the repository’s [citation
metadata](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/blob/main/CITATION.cff).

TDMM v0.2.0 is archived on Zenodo at
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23608508>. The historical v0.1.0 release
is archived at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20617705>.

TDMM is released under the [MIT
license](https://esrakurum.github.io/Bayesian-TDMM/LICENSE.md).

# Package index

## Fit and control

<!-- end list -->

  - `tdmm()` : Fit a time-dynamic mixed-effects model
  - `tdmm.control()` `tdmm_control()` : Computational controls for TDMM
    fits
  - `tdmm.priors()` : Family-specific default TDMM priors
  - `tdmm.parallel()` : Legacy parallel TDMM fitting wrapper

## Summaries, plots, and diagnostics

<!-- end list -->

  - `summary(<tdmm>)` : Summarize a fitted TDMM model
  - `plot(<tdmm>)` : Plot TDMM coefficient functions
  - `plot.trace(<tdmm>)` : Plot TDMM posterior traces
  - `recover.tdmm.betas.ci()` : Reconstruct TDMM coefficient-function
    intervals
  - `make.tdmm.plot.grid()` : Construct a TDMM plotting grid

## Data checks

<!-- end list -->

  - `check.bernoulli.balance()` : Check a binary Bernoulli response.
  - `check.gaussian.response()` : Check a numeric Gaussian response.
  - `check.poisson.counts()` : Check a nonnegative integer Poisson
    response.
  - `check.tdmm.data.structure()` : Check TDMM long-format input
    structure
  - `check.tdmm.family.data()` : Check TDMM data for an outcome family
  - `check.tdmm.subject.balance()` : Inspect subject visit counts

## Simulation helpers

<!-- end list -->

  - `data.gen.tdmm.bern()` : Generate a balanced-grid Bernoulli
    simulation dataset
  - `data.gen.tdmm.gauss()` : Generate a balanced-grid Gaussian
    simulation dataset
  - `data.gen.tdmm.pois()` : Generate a balanced-grid Poisson simulation
    dataset
